correctness.rationale: The explicitly defined Lobatto quadrature Q and Euler preconditioner D yield a rational recurrence. Exact matrix algebra gives the noninitial error-block trace/determinant and a conjugate eigenpair of modulus |z|/[2(2+|z|)]<1/2 for every real z<0, implying convergence to the stable Simpson collocation multiplier. In the stiff limit the affine two-stage fixed point (-1/2,1) and characteristic polynomial t^2-(11/12)t+1/4 yield e_K=-2^(1-K) sin(K theta)/sin(theta), theta=arccos(11/12). A root-of-unity algebraic-integer argument proves theta/pi irrational, and irrational-circle equidistribution gives natural density 1/2. Exact rational recurrence proves first stiff overshoot at K=8 (35934757/35831808), and independent exact direct sweeps prove R_8(-5000)>1. The standalone verifier passes 114 exact checks; the infinite theorem does not depend on enumeration.

value.rationale: The failure mechanism is not a cosmetic timestep substitution: for a widely used implicit-Euler SDC sweeper, an inner iteration which converges geometrically for every decaying scalar mode can still produce a finite-sweep integrator that grows on sufficiently stiff modes for a positive-density half of all sweep counts. The sharp first index and density theorem diagnose a genuine fixed-iteration-count selection hazard and show why convergence of correction sweeps cannot replace stability analysis of the end-step map. The result is narrowly but naturally tied to the standard three-node Lobatto stability benchmark; no nonlinear generality is claimed.
